notes.title: 🎄Festive Notice to all Leaders - Rawcember has arrived!🎅
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/a9f295d3c9c88696aceffca6d51e2eb33c3cd329.gif[/img]
“Jingle, jingle…”🔔

Do you hear this lovely sound, Leaders? 

It’s the delicate chime of the winter bells - which indicates that today is the first day of December! But, as the old legend goes, no December is merely a month in our beautiful Kingdom…

Dear Leaders, prepare your hearts as we invite you for this grand commencing - an event of unparalleled magnificence that will fill the season with incredible joy fit for the cool kids!

And the name of that event is
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/cd705518746fcb620ad3b95b806e5d8aa9da622e.png[/img]
The gates swing wide open to reveal this figure-of-speech winter wonderland! All of Raw Fury games and the team behind them come together to celebrate each other and, as the Kingdom team, we would like to share some of our fireplace stories about personal experiences with creating Kingdom✨

The most fantastic part of this month-long event is that it’s only the beginning! Expect more news, collaborations, streams, giveaways and exciting activities, some of which coming up as soon as later today🔥

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/ce5ea4da53e687c26d03ab5aa9447c07c115f511.png[/img]

[h2][b]Join us around a cozy fireplace - it’s story time with the devs✨[/b][/h2]

[i][h3]Immerse yourself in stories that transcend time, weaving a tapestry of magic and adventure. Let the written word be a lantern guiding you through the labyrinth of imagination.[/h3][/i]

[i]“Before all character sprites were done, we would put cats in the game as placeholders! My other favorite is the randomly rotating stuff... like when the mule just decides it walks on its face.”[/i] Alan, Game Designer

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/2ca753d7db6a729973166899518aab478efe4b9f.png[/img]

[i]“My fav bug is the one where you can get a duplicate dog. Two dogs. That’s a “not-a-bug-it’s-a-feature” bug, if I ever saw one.”[/i] Angelica, Experience Producer

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/016cca98585be0a4d7781938ca5c464a095013f0.jpg[/img]
[i]“Three winters ago, I joined the Kingdom team and one of the first things I got to do was play Kingdom Two Crowns in co-op together with Gordon Van Dyke. He taught me a Kingdom hack I never would have figured out on my own - if you upgrade your castle several levels fast, you get your first walls and wall upgrades for free! It was a privilege to learn from the best.”[/i] Elisabeth, Producer

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/912d95198d530111339faa65fb0c425a541ea18e.png[/img]
“[i]I think my favorite bug has to be in Shogun when you chop down a tree a ninja was hiding behind, he wouldn't mind and just stood there hiding in plain sight😅But being so well-trained, he pulled it off, and the Greed would walk right past him anyway. 
P.S. I'm not even sure anymore, if we fixed this or not, I think we did.[/i]” Danijel, Developer

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/22ddf9751bbd4a10aa955c18ffa439cebd23cc43.png[/img]
“[i]When I joined the Kingdom team as a QA I was told to just play the game for the first couple of weeks to learn it. This liberty allowed me to figure out one of the known, but unreproducible issues. That was my first ticket in Jira and remains one of my favorite bugs to this day.😊 It was this peasant who moved like they were waterskiing. I called it "a slider".

It was challenging to reproduce and it took me about a week of playtesting to figure it out. Eventually, I exposed it!

The issue would happen when a floater would pick up a peasant and then when archers would kill the floater, the peasant would drop and remain frozen in this animation, sliding their way until they would pick up a tool and become an employed citizen.😊[/i]"Kristina, QA Manager

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/659dc112249897ed3bb5c2271fff86e537c75640.png[/img]
[i]“Now with the Christmas season coming and the snow already laying on the streets, I can’t help but imagine what it would be like to just hang out with my colleagues in Christmas jumpers, have some hot chocolate and gingerbread cookies, then altogether gather in the Gaming Room, and just play the Two Crowns co-op with one another😊”[/i] Driver, Senior Community Manager

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/6fdbd9093cbd27802cabd29761bfa7e0fb24ff8f.png[/img]

[i]“My favourite thing is playing the Christmas Event in Kingdom New Lands. No matter how many times I play it, it still makes me so happy to get to prance around on a reindeer and drop presents. I absolutely love Christmas and this never fails to get me in the festive mood.

The thing I recently discovered is that, if presents drop near the Greed, they'll take those in place of a coin and it's actually so cute seeing a little Greed holding a present.”[/i] Vicki, Community Ambassador

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967186/4840bd3fb2ae0cd5c6a3c4524d3f68a2f6eca282.jpg[/img] 

[h3]Share your cozy Kingdom stories with us in the comments to this post!🤗[/h3]

And don’t forget to subscribe to our social channels as Rawcember is just starting to unveil its treasures🎁

notes.title: Save & Sound festival is now on!🎶
notes.content:
Imagine a world where leg warmers, mullets, and boomboxes were the height of fashion, and the air was filled with infectious beats of synth-pop and new wave… Kingdom Eighties takes you on an immersive nostalgic trip through a vividly recreated '80s, complete with iconic fashion, classic lemonade stands and arcades, but most importantly and something that we celebrate today, the music that defined the time and breathed life into our singleplayer adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/445a5229148c7d2836757ad160f6b7414f27e122.jpg[/img]

The '80s music soundtrack is the beating heart of the game, and we've dedicated an extraordinary amount of effort and passion into tailoring a truly exceptional '80s-inspired soundtrack that serves as the time machine transporting players back to this iconic era. With painstaking care and attention, we've delved into the vast treasure of '80s iconic musical waves, painstakingly assembling a collection of tracks that encapsulate the essence of every level. Each song has been hand-crafted to evoke unique emotions, memories and nostalgia that define the '80s experience, as well as form strong connections and associations with each of the locations in the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/5d11317c6a3f55d63f537308c2d176b99dfcc54a.gif[/img]

Our soundtrack is more than just a playlist - it's a carefully woven tapestry of experiences you encounter when playing Kingdom Eighties, and a symphony of synthesizers and electric guitars that capture the spectrum of emotions from exploring dark forests and cycling around your camp grounds to battling ferocious waves of Greed. Whether it's the infectious beats of synth-pop or the enigmatic allure of new wave, every note has been thoughtfully selected to immerse players in the vibrant spirit of the era and the dynamics of the gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/1d3527799c80224277b7b112ff194d402beb8ed4.gif[/img]

The headmaster of this extraordinary soundtrack is a renowned composer Andreas Hald who is himself a passionate devotee of '80s music. Andreas has intertwined his incredible talent with love for the ‘80s which resulted in the beautiful recreation of the era’ authentic soundscapes, ensuring that every drum machine beat, every guitar riff and every synth’s harmony resonates with the spirit of the ‘80s summer camps, exploration and mystery, as well as perfectly synchronizes with the gameplay. This meticulous synchronization allows the soundtrack to dynamically adapt to the player's actions in the game, creating an immersive experience where the music doesn't just accompany the playthrough but also plays an integral role in shaping the story and ultimately immersing into it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/9760f3569fa78ce760ce0c152c91e23c47ce388a.png[/img]

Tonight at 8pm at the [url=https://www.saveandsound.io/]Save & Sound festival[/url], you’ll have a unique chance to observe Andreas being immersed and fully dedicated to the careful arrangement of notes and sounds that, when assembled together, create the mesmerizing Kingdom Eighties’ soundtrack. Don’t miss your chance to see how the game’s melodies - the beating heart, the driving force and the soul of the entire gaming experience - come to life. You will witness how every note, every chord and every key become a time capsule, a portal to an exciting ‘80s gameplay that captures hearts and transports players on an unforgettable journey back in time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/de66d0ed259ed0b480d12df0af2e22c5a4f17ed1.png[/img]

We hope to see you there for this very personal and enchanting experience! And make sure you follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/kingdomthegame]Twitter (X)[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/kingdomthegame/]Facebook[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/rawfury/]Instagram[/url], [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@rawfurygames]TikTok[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/GcRfrNUM]Discord[/url] to make sure you never miss special events like this one💜

notes.title: Patch Updates 1.0.1
notes.content:
[h3]Hey campers! 
[/h3]

We’re so happy to see so many of you enjoying Kingdom Eighties. In today’s update, we’re bringing you a patch that will eliminate some of the most urgent bugs and issues that you’ve reported to us from your playthroughs. 

[b]General fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Your archers will now defend your entire Kingdom if there is a Blood Moon and a Retaliation Wave happening simultaneously, instead of stacking at the Blood Moon side only. 
[*] Your archers will no longer sometimes stop attacking while taking part in a Siege assault. 
[*] The Champ no longer gets stuck in a running animation when you pay to activate the Siege Dumpster just before exiting a cave.
[*] Fixed an issue that prevented players from picking up their dropped crown after loading a save.
[*] Greed portals should no longer spawn so close to the camp that you are prevented from building your innermost wall. Let us know if the problem persists when you generate a new map!
[/list]

[b]Episode specific fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] The Champ’s trophy event in Episode I will now always trigger correctly when paid for.
[*] Exiting the cave in Episode I without your crown will now trigger game loss correctly, instead of causing a freeze.
[*] The Tinkerer can no longer get stuck in a walking animation by the cave in Episode III.
[*] The workers will no longer drop the canoe as soon as the Siege Dumpster is destroyed or abandoned in the cave in Episode I, which would sometimes leave the canoe out of reach.
[*] Fixed an issue that would cause the player to be stuck in the cave after fulfilling the victory conditions in Episode IV.
[*] You can now leave the cave in Episode IV at any time, allowing you to regroup and try again after a failed Siege assault.
[/list]

[b]Achievement fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] “County Connection” will now trigger correctly in all episodes.
[*] “Saw Boss” will now trigger correctly in Episode IV.
[*] “Loner” will now trigger correctly in Episode IV. 
[*] “George Burnett Had Twins” will now trigger correctly in Episode IV.
[/list]

[h3]We’ll have another update to Eighties ready for you after the dev team has returned from their summer holidays. Stay tuned![/h3]

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Recruiting the kids in Kingdom Eighties
notes.content:
[h3]Development team checking in! Are you guys up for some sneak peeks?[/h3]

[b]In this week’s blog, we're getting familiarized with Kingdom Eighties' take on a classic Kingdom mechanic - your loyal subjects.  [/b]

As a ruler in Kingdom Two Crowns, you would grow your Kingdom by recruiting new citizens from encampments out in the woods. But in Kingdom Eighties, we’re shaking things up. This time around, your ruler is a teenage camp counselor that is joined by tiny, but brave, kids. So what kind of a town would Monarch be if there were homeless kids living in makeshift tents everywhere? Nah, we couldn't really have that. So we ended up choosing different buildings for each location. At summer camp, kids hang around outside their cabins, and in the suburbs, the playground is the place to be. Among the bustling shops of Main Street, you’ll find kids by the doorstep of the shoe shops - just waiting for adventure (that’s you!) to pick 'em up. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/dff19a0ce3dd9ecb88e15effd6bf47d5f0e319cb.png[/img]

Here's where things got a bit tricky for the development team. With the recruitment buildings looking different in every location, how could we make sure that the player always knew where to find the kids? We needed a visual clue to help guide the players. 

The solution came when one of our designers remembered something he used to see as a kid. Shoes tied together by the laces and tossed over power lines. A symbol for both celebration and rebellion - these stinky, outgrown sneakers were exactly what we needed. So if you ever find yourself in need of more kids to join you in the battle against the Greed - now you know what to look for!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/eb5c5eb6ec019ee5144b780cb2fd6147c9235d76.gif[/img]

[i]But there's more! Let's talk about putting those kids to work! Not in a “child labor” kinda way, more of a "let's get shit done because the greed is invading our neighborhood" kinda way.[/i]

A new feature in Kingdom Eighties is that the kids will not only do things like build walls, shoot arrows or chop down trees. They are also eager to earn pocket money by doing chores around the Kingdom, such as mowing the lawn, taking care of dirty dishes in the mess tent, or pawning off old knick-knacks at a yard sale. Anything to earn a buck or two, no task is too small for the savvy kids of Camp Kingdom!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/f94461437f7dbfbc3c17c8669be812662bf9db54.gif[/img]

[h3]We will be talking more about the kids, the buildings, and what will make Kingdom Eighties a fresh new take on the series on our social media channels. Don’t forget to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/kingdomthegame]Twitter[/url]![/h3]

notes.title: Interview with Andreas Hald, composer for Kingdom Eighties, Part Two!
notes.content:
Development team calling!

A couple of weeks ago, we introduced you to the composer of Kingdom Eighties, Andreas Hald, and gave you a peek into how his mind works when creating the music for the game. This week, Andreas takes us even deeper into his process and nerds out about synthesizers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/a07fa92ee80303729f30dcd6c4d57407301bc8f6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/c8f68fbcbfee7e9633881e794ec33f00498d3893.png[/img]

[b]How do you achieve the sound of the 1980s?[/b]
I think the most important elements of ‘80s music are the synthesizers, arpeggios, gated reverbs, sequencers, drum machines, tape echoes, cassette recorders, and something called FM. It stands for frequency modulation, which is a type of sound that you can get out of synthesizers. It was extremely popular in the early ‘80s, so that’s why you hear a lot of FM sound in the music of that era.

Furthermore, and I don’t mean this in a demeaning way, a lot of the music from the ‘80s was somewhat simple harmonically. I have a degree as a jazz musician, but bringing in some of those complex chords and structures just wouldn’t make sense for this soundtrack. 

So the interesting stuff happened in the textures and the sounds. Maybe back then you were limited by, for example, a drum machine with mediocre samples because it only had a small memory buffer, as well as somewhat basic sequencers. Or maybe that sequencer or the synthesizer was difficult to program. So I wanted to keep that in my music by limiting myself by using the same gear from that era and trying not to cheat. 

My not-so-secret weapons are delays and echoes. You can take the most boring and basic synth sound but if you run it through a delay, you instantly get magic. And then you use the delays and the echoes like instruments. You play with them, you move the knobs around or you touch the tape with your fingers to do small pitch things. 

I’ve done a lot like that to get that ‘80s vibe, but at times it’s actually kind of modern-sounding as well. In order to create the darker side of the score - for example the Blood Moon cue - all the textures that I can’t create on a limited classic ‘80s synth, I’ve used a more modern, modular synthesizer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/87fd622d5348d7d95fc31c38a90be603331f018a.png[/img]

[b]What were your main inspirations when composing the Kingdom Eighties soundtrack?[/b]
I’ve honestly tried to steer away from listening to music for direct inspiration because I try not to be too colored in my choices. That’s a really difficult thing to do. But I’ve listened to this kind of music my whole life and I am an ‘80s guy at heart, so if I had to name some inspirations it would be Tangerine Dream, Vangelis, and John Carpenter, tv shows like He-Man and Knight Rider, as well as pop music by artists like Cyndi Lauper. The wailing, crying guitars that play in harmony in rock music - I love that, so I have that in there as well. 

I also had the early graphics and storyline in front of me when composing. I like to darken my studio and only have lights from my gear, a few soft lamps, and maybe even turn some lava lamps on. It’s just something that gets me in the mood - the dark environment and the pictures in front of me.

But the main inspiration comes from my gear. I’ve been collecting synths for a very long time and I have a huge range of classic synthesizers from the ‘80s, but I’ve never really quite gotten to use them as much as I really wanted in my film composing work. Then this project came along and it felt like something I couldn’t let slip away from me because it was just up my alley.

I very quickly decided that this was a project where I wanted to record everything outside of the computer, through hardware synthesizers, hardware recording equipment, and tape recorders, and keep it analog, organic, and human. I’m playing everything myself. And I’ve tried to do that for as long as possible before committing it to tape and recording it on the computer. 

Of course, I bought a new synthesizer for this project alone - the Oberheim OB-X8. It’s a new synth based on a very old synth from the ‘80s which money can’t buy. The Oberheim is known for its voice panning, which means that the synthesizer alternates between the speakers for each note. So when you play a note, it first plays in the left speaker, and then you play another note and it plays in the right speaker, spreading the synth across the stereo spectrum. It makes many people go “oh, I can hear it’s an Oberheim”. It’s kind of weird, but it’s something that I really, really dig about it. I’ve used the Oberhiem extensively throughout Eighties and there is one track where you can hear it prominently - during foggy days there is a song played with only that synthesizer. 

So I would say that the music in Kingdom Eighties is an homage to those artists as well as to the classic synthesizers from that era. It has to be the most enjoyable project I’ve worked on so far. I’ve been given so much trust and in return, it has boosted my ambition for this project through the roof. It’s really nice to have that freedom. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/a07fa92ee80303729f30dcd6c4d57407301bc8f6.png[/img]

Thanks for reading part 2 of Andreas' interview! We’ll be sharing more info about the Kingdom OST further down the line. See more of Andreas' work here: http://andreashald.com/  

Until next time, why not follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/kingdomthegame]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/kingdomthegame/]Facebook[/url] or chat in our [url=https://discord.gg/rawfury%5DDiscord%5B/url%5D?]Discord[/url]?

notes.title: Progress Blog #2 - April Update
notes.content:
Hey there, my name is Vladimir, and I'm part of the programming team here at Fury Studios, blogging at you [strike]live[/strike] asynchronously from beautiful Zagreb, Croatia. Today I'll share more about what we've been up to in the last couple of months. You've probably guessed that this post is going to get more technical, but fret not; all the techno-babble results in some wonderful upgrades to the look of Kingdom. But you won't have to trust me on that; I come bearing gifs!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/10560dfabd813b39e93c3579d25ccfb33a54698b.gif[/img]
[i]Today is a gift, that's why they call it the Present![/i]

[h2][b]Today I'll focus on a new effect we added to Kingdom Eighties: Emission.[/b][/h2]

Emission is best described as a property of an object to glow independently, highlighting itself and objects around it. It's achieved by drawing pixels that should emit a glow into a separate texture and then adding that to our final image. Since it's all done dynamically, it allows us to play with the intensity, color, and spread of the glow to achieve the look we feel is perfect for Kingdom Eighties. Plus, it's fun to add to different objects in the game and see what a rad glow-in-the-dark deer would look like.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/f212c2719c83a8637ae688b53193242b1be9b666.gif[/img]
[i]Ghost Glow Intensity Example
[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/578cdb01847d9fc180bebf14b2a17de783fcc602.gif[/img]
[i]Ghost Glow Color Example
[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/2d681d7b9c82d5527d16ee573ade5183f2266ddd.gif[/img]
[i]Deer Glowing in the Forest
[/i]

[h3][b]So why add this to Kingdom? And why now?

Two reasons.[/b][/h3]

Kingdom has that "wow" factor in its presentation, and a lot of that comes down to the water and reflections, combined with the crisp pixel art. We knew we could expand our palette of visual effects and make it even more enjoyable to boot up a Kingdom game and just vibe out.

[b]Kingdom Eighties is special and stands apart from other Kingdom games and settings.[/b] While I know the 80s aren't exactly "modern times", our comparison points are the knights and vikings of Two Crowns, so I'll just go ahead and call this a Modern Setting. And so we've included a lot of sprites of modern architecture, some of which glow. Ferris wheels, shop signs, street lights... notes.title: Interview with Andreas Hald, composer for Kingdom Eighties, Part One!
notes.content:
Development team calling!

We hope you've enjoyed peeking behind the curtains for Kingdom Eighties so far. This week, we want to share the first part of the conversation we had with Andreas Hald, who is the composer of the Kingdom Eighties soundtrack. Andreas is a Copenhagen-based film and media composer who has written scores for movies, television and lots more, and we're super happy to have him on board for Eighties. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/3dfafcf2062f8ce079cea41f8bc1e846d1eacf31.png[/img]

[previewyoutube=qHImGS-YJ5E;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]What are the defining points of a Kingdom OST to you? [/b]
For previous Kingdom games’ soundtracks, the defining points to me have been ambience, sparse, almost like a melting pot of all sorts of different musical elements being put together in order to create something else than your typical genre-specific music. It’s music that, at least to me, sometimes might sound odd but in a very good way. To me, that is classic Kingdom - that melting pot of elements being put together. 

Then you have Kingdom Eighties which is a different beast. This game relies heavily on memories and references of 1980s Americana. The eighties were fast-paced, you had acid-washed jeans and the neon colors - very bombastic and in your face with most things. There was also this shift in technology which opened up new sonic environments, so we had to come up with something else for Kingdom Eighties than what you hear in the previous Kingdom games. You want it to sound like the ‘80s but at the same time like a Kingdom game, so how do you balance that?

It is a tough one to crack. The ‘80s sounds one way to me but it may sound completely different to you based on your memories, what you listened to, and where you were brought up. Did we want it to reference glam rock, hip hop, or electronic synthesizer music? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/0f1589cd7b1dbacede2326c88800edb8e5f6fc09.jpg[/img]

If you go a bit further with it, a Kingdom soundtrack should enhance the player experience and not step on the players’ toes too much. It’s there to make the game feel more immersive and I think that the music kind of reflects on the anatomy of the game. It is two-dimensional, you can only go left or right, and it forces you to be creative in both the design of the game but also in the design of the music. You need to make it interesting, evolving and cool, but within the boundaries of the core of Kingdom.

I think Kingdom Eighties is just a different paced game from previous Kingdom games, which I think is cool, but it is different and you need to embrace that and go with it. I think that we’ve gone all the way to create an ‘80s game in all aspects, not just the music, and I think that’s how it should be. No half-measures. Go all the way, full out. Be brave and don’t look back.

Thanks for reading and tune in later this month where we continue with part 2 of Andreas' interview! 
See more of Andreas' work here: [url=https://andreashald.com/]https://andreashald.com/[/url]

Development team calling! 

In last week’s blog, we talked a bit about the level structure of Kingdom Eighties. Now, it’s time to get familiar with the very first level of the game: [b]Camp Kingdom.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/2206928e6087142d54c9e260237cdab590ac10e3.jpg[/img]

Camp Kingdom is the year's highlight for kids of all ages in the town of Monarch. This year, the Leader had been looking forward to working as a camp counsellor once again while taking a break from the escalating arguments between their parents. And sure, camp started out great, with fun outdoor activities, chores in the mess tent, and slow evenings by the campfire. 

But something is nagging at the Leader. They’re not sure if the funny feeling is caused by the tensions at home or the strange sightings in the nearby woods. But rest assured; they’re about to find out. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/86df3b0a38b1a17c7cf47d7939a9328f22cb1150.png[/img]

When the game starts, you assume control of The Leader, who has just discovered that strange creatures attack the camp at night. These attackers, which experienced Kingdom players will recognize as the Greed, break down walls and steal utilities. With no one answering the phone at home, the kids at the camp have to band together to defend themselves and escape the attacks. The skills they’ve honed at the archery range will be put to the ultimate test. There’s just one problem: the strange creatures have stolen their only means of escape - the canoes. 

It’s up to The Leader now. As the player, you will coordinate the kids at the camp to build fortifications, gather resources and ultimately get the canoes back. Some of the older kids around Camp Kingdom could provide specialized skills. The Tinkerer and The Champ are hiding nearby, but it will take some extra persuasion for them to join the effort. 

The Summer of Greed starts at Camp Kingdom, but it doesn’t end there! We’ll have more to share soon. Until next time!

notes.title: No Islands!? Where does our journey take us?
notes.content:
Development team calling!

We're grateful for the patience and the excitement you have shown for Kingdom Eighties so far. To keep you in the loop on what's to come, we'll start sharing more and more blog posts like this one on the road toward launch.

There is so much we want to tell you about the game, so let us start from the beginning - the locations!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/3dfafcf2062f8ce079cea41f8bc1e846d1eacf31.png[/img]

Experienced Monarchs will already be familiar with the levels of Kingdom. The campaigns of New Lands and Two Crowns encouraged you to build, explore, defend, and conquer up to six islands across your realm. These islands all share a common theme, which we expanded on with the addition of new settings in Kingdom Two Crowns.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/9ea68aad5c4d67818d16eb3ea08e5fd539c6ba45.png[/img]
[i]A familar view when playing Kingdom Two Crowns[/i]

In Kingdom Eighties, things work a little bit differently.

The Leader's journey to save the town of Monarch starts at Camp Kingdom, a level that you might have spotted already in early gameplay footage. In the previous games, the player was allowed to travel back and forth between islands; the Leader's story will take them on a one-way journey through four distinct locations.

This change has required the team to rethink how these levels were built. In the previous games, the player was allowed to travel back and forth between islands to unlock secrets and battle the Greed in their own preferred order. The linear progression of Eighties demands a different approach which dives into the motivations of the Monarch and the Greed. As a narrative driven experience, each place has it's own flow and unique events, objectives, and layouts. The Monarch may need to escape the area, complete a quest, or even make substantial sacrifices for the greater good.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/3dfafcf2062f8ce079cea41f8bc1e846d1eacf31.png[/img]

In the coming months, we'll show you more from some of these locations to give you a better idea. But for now we're working on getting our canoe back, stolen by those pesky Greed!

notes.title: Progress Blog #1 - Why we delayed to 2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/6aa8789eaaf75d77ecd6971fbfb09c31a9bf2b26.jpg[/img]

Monarchs! Here are some lines from Gordon Van Dyke, the ruler of the Kingdom himself! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/3dfafcf2062f8ce079cea41f8bc1e846d1eacf31.png[/img]

As artists in the video game industry, we understand the excitement that comes with the anticipation of a new game's release. However, as much as we all want to play the latest and greatest as soon as possible, there are sometimes reasons for delay that are beyond our control.

Our reason for delaying was the need for additional time to perfect the game. As artists, we want our work to be the best it can be, and sometimes that means taking a little extra time to get it just right. Whether it's fixing bugs, tweaking the gameplay mechanics, improving the story, or adding additional content, a delay can give us the opportunity to make sure the final experience is the best it can be.

It can be frustrating to have to wait longer for a game to be released, but I hope that you can understand that these delays are often necessary for the team to deliver the best possible experience for players. We want our work to be something that you will enjoy for years to come, and a little extra time can make all the difference in achieving that goal.

A video game delay is never a decision made lightly. It's important to remember that behind every game is a team of artists, programmers, and designers who are all dedicated to delivering the best experience possible in Kingdom Eighties. So, while the wait may be longer, we have no doubt that the delay will be worth it, and we’re getting closer and closer to an end result to be proud of.

notes.content:
Thank you to everyone who joined us at Gamescom. We were thrilled to show off some Kingdom Eighties gameplay and loved hearing your feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42371416/4f4b79a6201ee83fe7ebd5295f68c186730568aa.jpg[/img]

We'll be at PAX West this week if you want to have a go yourself ([b]Level 4, Booth 745![/b])  But if you can't make it, that's okay; we have a little sneak peek of the gameplay right here:

[previewyoutube=QlhqHuPUsr4;full][/previewyoutube]

We also have a message to share from the top Monarch himself! 👑

[b]Gordon Van Dyke:[/b] [i]The backstory [of Kingdom Eighties]; you’re a camp counselor when these mysterious creatures attack, you’re given a Crown of Creation to lead the kids to defeat the Greed and save your town and families. Along the adventure you recruit some npc friends who will join the adventure as you battle your way from camp to the town, and the finally standoff with the Greed. 

The motivation for the summer camp was for the story with the bonus it would feel familiar to Kingdom players, and a solid setting for new players to learn the mechanics. Once you escape the summer camp to your suburban neighborhood is where the settings really change taking you somewhere very new for each level.

Why the 80s? I was 5 to 15 through the 80s, so the location and references to the 80s comes from my own childhood. 😊[/i]

Keep your eyes peeled for more blogs and streams in the future!

notes.title: Kingdom Eighties - A summer of Greed awaits in Kingdom Eighties!
notes.content:
Everyone knows the coolest decade was the 1980’s, right? The coolest cartoons, the coolest movies, the coolest TV shows. And Kingdom is the coolest indie strategy series out there. So, how about we put all that cool stuff together… 

[b]Raw Fury[/b] and Developer [b]Fury Studios[/b] are excited to reveal the newest title of the award-winning Kingdom-Series: [b]Kingdom Eighties[/b], a story driven love letter to 1980’s Americana, but which is still very much a Kingdom game. 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1956040/Kingdom_Eighties/][/url]

[previewyoutube=srq0fgpX9F0;full][/previewyoutube]
Wishlist today and be RADICAL: 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1956040/Kingdom_Eighties/

When the mysterious Greed threatens a small middle-American town, a rag-tag band of brave kids are dragged in to an epic struggle of seemingly insurmountable odds to save their families, their neighborhood and their town. 

[b]Kingdom Eighties[/b] is a newly developed game within the popular Kingdom-series and will surprise experienced players, newcomers to the series, as well as anyone that remembers sitting around in their pajamas on a Saturday morning in front of the television. 

[b]Kingdom Eighties[/b] will be released on the coolest platforms later this year. To learn more about Kingdom visit the official website: https://www.kingdomthegame.com/
